story_title: [TEST ONLY — duplicate-click test] V17 grammar stress test — every remaining path

slides.headline: 94% of breaches start with one email.
slides.body: Not a zero-day. Not malware. A single click.

slides.headline: How one click becomes a full compromise.
slides.body: Click — credential capture — session token stolen — internal network — lateral movement — full compromise.

slides.headline: The layers a request has to pass through.
slides.body: Client — API gateway — auth layer — application server — database.

slides.headline: The startup spent $2,400,000 chasing the wrong fix.
slides.body: They spent every dollar on the wrong patch and had nothing to show for it — new firewall — pen test contract — compliance audit — breach anyway.

slides.headline: How fast this category actually grew.
slides.body: In 2019 it was a research paper. By 2021 the first commercial product shipped. In 2023 every major cloud vendor added native support. By 2025 it was the industry default.

slides.headline: The evidence trail nobody followed up on.
slides.body: A quiet commit changed the auth check.
slides.context: First flagged in a routine audit

slides.headline: Patched vs unpatched systems, six months later.
slides.body: The gap compounds faster than most teams expect.
slides.context: Breach rate 2%, mean time to detect 4 hours, average cost $40,000
slides.implication: Breach rate 41%, mean time to detect 197 days, average cost $4,200,000

slides.headline: Everyone thinks bigger companies are safer targets to avoid.
slides.body: Actually, attackers prefer them — more third-party vendors means more doors.

slides.headline: Security is a habit, not a product.
One click is still the whole story.
slides.body: Save this before your team needs it.
